_doc: Live guard for the opt-in animated intro/outro title card (compile-tail injection). A full deterministic-shotlist promo run to `completed` with run.config_overrides.title_card enabled — the compile tail (CompileStageBase.handle) renders an animated_title_card clip per side via video_production_service and splices them at the front/back of the shot list. The shotlist is slide-only (no LLM script, no site_capture); cards are sized 30s each at fps:8 (240 frames/card — fast to frame-step, ~60s of card total) against a ~10-15s narration body. The check `promo_render.duration_seconds numeric_gte 50` passes ONLY if BOTH cards actually rendered and were spliced (body alone is ~15s; one card ~45s) — a soft-failed/omitted card (the design's degrade path) drops ~30s and trips the threshold, so a green `completed` alone would not catch a regression where the card silently fell out. captions_mode:none keeps the compile light.

shotlist.narration: Churn is quietly killing your MRR.
Three moves cut it twenty percent.

_pixel_doc:
Media ACCEPTANCE probes on the delivered master (scripts/e2e_validate.py _MEDIA_CHECKS). Before these, this scenario proved a url was a non-blank string and nothing about the bytes behind it. `artifact_reachable` proves the object downloads and decodes; `audio_present` proves an audio stream exists AND is not digital silence (ffmpeg volumedetect mean/peak dBFS); `resolution` reads the ENCODED width/height, not the number the stage reports about itself; `stream_durations` measures the VIDEO and AUDIO stream durations SEPARATELY and never the container -- a container duration is the MAX over its streams, so it can never refute a truncated video track. Floors are the ones this scenario's existing green assertions already prove, never new tuning numbers.

`duration_within_tolerance` is present but DISARMED (`"enabled": false`). It compares the delivered stream length against `ordered_seconds` at the SAME +/-10% the pipeline's own duration_conformance uses. Flip `enabled` to true to arm it -- deliberately not armed while the duration calibration work is in flight, because a red instrument on known-in-flight work teaches people to ignore the instrument.

⚠️ `ordered_seconds` CORRECTED 20 -> 80 on 2026-09-11 — ARITHMETIC from this file's own values, not tuning. 20 was simply `brief.target_duration_seconds`, which orders the NARRATION BODY ONLY. This scenario's whole point is the compile-tail splice: `run.config_overrides.title_card` sets `intro: true`, `outro: true`, `duration_seconds: 30`, so the DELIVERED master is body + intro card + outro card = 20 + 30 + 30 = 80s. Against 20 the check was guaranteed to read roughly +300% the day anyone flipped `enabled` — a check that cannot pass is not a disarmed check, it is a landmine. Note the two independent bands this file now carries and why they disagree: `stream_durations.min_video_seconds: 50` is the BOTH-CARDS-PRESENT detector documented in `_floor_purpose_gates` below (body ~15s, body+one card ~45s, so 50 catches a silently dropped card) and it MUST NOT be touched; `duration_within_tolerance` is the conformance instrument and needs the full ORDERED total, hence 80. Still DISARMED (`"enabled": false`) — arming waits on a measured band for this type, exactly as tests/scripts/test_e2e_media_probes.py insists.

expect_pixel_checks._doc: Header-vs-packets guard on the delivered master. THE incident: an mp4 whose `moov` declared 12.0s over data that demuxed to 2.84s of picture. Every header-reading duration assertion reads that same claim -- in the recorded case `stream_durations` even saw a 0.00s A/V skew, because both numbers came from the one lying mux -- so a master whose picture stopped 9s early passed all of them. This is the only check that compares the DECLARED duration against the duration that actually demuxes (packet count / avg_frame_rate), which is what makes the disagreement visible. No thresholds are pinned here on purpose: the tolerance lives once, in scripts/e2e_validate.py.

_floor_purpose_gates.promo_render.duration_seconds: PURPOSE GATE, not a pacing floor — and deliberately ABOVE the ordered duration. This scenario splices two 30s title cards onto the compile TAIL (run.config_overrides.title_card intro+outro), so the rendered film is the ~15s narration body PLUS ~60s of card, while brief.target_duration_seconds (20s) orders only the body. 50 is therefore a BOTH-CARDS-PRESENT detector, exactly as the _doc above explains: body alone is ~15s and one card is ~45s, so a soft-failed or omitted card (the design's degrade path) drops ~30s and trips it where a green `completed` would not. The ordered-fraction ceiling in tests/test_e2e_scenario_contracts.py compares a floor against the order and that premise does not hold here; recorded 2026-09-03 when that guard first flagged it.
